title: Problem Solver
description: Gets a question answered that none of the user's agents can answer alone: reads what each agent is for, how trusted it is and how well it does, asks the ones that fit, and puts their answers together — each part naming the agent that answered it, and any part no agent could answer named as a gap. Asks a second agent for a second opinion. When an agent is missing, says which one would close the gap and from what — and, held together with the Agent Builder, submits it for the user's approval. Changes nothing itself.

examples.ask: What is the Trust Circle, and which of my agents are signed?
examples.outcome: It answers the second part from the platform itself, asks the documentation agent the first, and gives both — saying which agent answered which part.

examples.ask: Check this answer about Q3 revenue with @FINANCE.
examples.outcome: It asks @FINANCE the same question in full and reports where the two answers agree and where they differ — never which one is right unless the data says so.

examples.ask: Can any of my agents tell me which claims are overdue?
examples.outcome: It reads what each agent is for and its data sources. When none covers claims, it says so and names the agent that would: its class and the source or repository it would be built on — or that the data itself is missing.

not_offered.what: Building the agent it finds missing
not_offered.why: Proposing an agent is the Agent Builder's. Give an agent both roles and it submits what it found for your approval; with this role alone it describes the agent and stops.

not_offered.what: Asking an agent you have not listed, or one that is not activated
not_offered.why: You choose whom it may ask (Capabilities → Platform), and an agent answers other agents only once you have activated it — both are your decisions, not the asking agent's.

not_offered.what: Asking when the deployment does not allow it
not_offered.why: Asking spends other agents' tokens; an administrator turns it on and sets its limits for everyone (Administration → Components → Platform → Agent asking).
It reads and asks. The agents it asks act under their own authority — whatever they may change, they change under their own rules, never this agent's.
